query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Creating a gradient nanostructured surface layer in a conventional metal can concurrently improve both its strength and ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: A conventional coarse-grained metal with homogeneous microstructure.
generation.intervention: Application of a severe plastic deformation technique (e.g., surface mechanical attrition treatment) to form a gradient nanograined layer on the surface.
generation.conditions: Standard room temperature tensile testing; the gradient layer is maintained on a sufficiently thick sample such that the core remains relatively coarse-grained.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous gradient in grain size from a nanostructured surface to a coarse-grained interior.
generation.mechanism: The nanograined surface increases yield strength by hindering dislocation motion, while the gradient in grain size promotes heterogeneous strain distribution and strain hardening, enhancing ductility by smoothly transferring deformation from the stiff surface to the ductile core.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to a uniformly coarse-grained or uniformly nanostructured metal, the gradient nanostructured metal will exhibit both an increased yield strength and improved uniform elongation.
generation.baseline: Uniformly processed coarse-grained metal or a uniformly nanostructured metal without a gradient.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected to be effective provided that the gradient layer is of sufficient thickness relative to the sample size; effects may diminish if the gradient is too shallow or if the processing introduces defects.
generation.uncertainty: The relative magnitude of the improvements in strength and ductility will depend on processing parameters and material-specific responses, which are not fully quantified here.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare identical specimens of the metal in question. Process one set with a surface mechanical attrition treatment to form a gradient nanostructured layer, while leaving another set as a baseline with a uniform coarse-grained structure. Conduct tensile tests under identical conditions.
measurements: Microstructural characterization (e.g., grain size distribution via electron microscopy) to confirm the gradient
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated specimens do not show both a statistically significant increase in yield strength and an increase (or no decrease) in uniform elongation compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
